competency_fulfillment.rationale: Seed 50 asks 'Estimate how many unit tiles cover the square in all.' yet keys 16 against 15 and 17, so no actual estimate can pick the key; seed 45 repeats the pattern, asking 'About how many tiles in total will you use?' with 25 sitting beside 26. The tile-covering half of 'Illustrate and estimate' is genuinely done, but the estimating verb is only wording - every item is settled by exact counting.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both shapes the competency names are present and repeated: seed 44 'A square is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 2 rows and 2 columns.' and seed 606 'A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 4 rows and 7 columns.'; the illustrate verb is carried by picture items such as seed 55 'Look at the 4×3 array. How many squares are shaded in all?', and square cases run non-trivially from that 2 by 2 up to seed 45's 5 rows and 5 columns.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Nothing asks a Grade 3 Quarter 1 pupil to hold more than one step: seed 602 'You are laying unit square tiles over a rectangle, fitting 5 rows and 3 columns exactly.' states both counts outright, and the only narrative, seed 601's 'Pia wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 2 cm long and 3 cm wide with square tiles.', carries one actor and two numbers with no intervening arithmetic before the tile count.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four genuinely different stems appear rather than one skin: the declarative tiling of seed 42 'A rectangle is covered edge-to-edge with unit square tiles, arranged in 2 rows and 7 columns.', the second-person seed 45 'You are laying unit square tiles over a square, fitting 5 rows and 5 columns exactly.', the picture-read seed 605 'Look at the 5×6 array. How many squares are shaded in all?', and seed 601's garden narrative, spread across mcq, cloze and read_mcq.

competency_alignment.rationale: Seed 601 'Pia wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 2 cm long and 3 cm wide with square tiles. How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?' never fixes the side of the square tile, so the keyed 6 follows only if the reader silently assumes a 1 cm tile; it turns on centimetre measures rather than on the 'square tile units' this competency counts. Every other sample, e.g. seed 46's 2 rows and 5 columns, stays squarely on tile arrays.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Seed 500 'Look at the shaded shape. How many squares are shaded in all?' keys 100 against 97, 101 and 102, and its stem states no dimensions at all, so the pupil must enumerate a hundred squares from the picture and be exact to within one - the opposite of estimating. Every other item is comfortably sized for this grade, the largest being seed 605's 5×6 array at 30 and seed 43's 7 rows by 4 columns at 28.
